societies.name: The Hydrogen Sonata (Gzilt before Sublimation)

scope.period: The mature Gzilt society shortly before its collective Sublimation
scope.population: Biological Gzilt citizens, a disclosed humanlike population proxy
exclusions: A claim that rank automatically means daily productive work

societies.description:
The Gzilt have had enough material resources for their population for millennia. Money and private possessions survive, but money has largely lost its normal power to make someone struggle for necessities. This puts the material score well toward provision, even though the society retains structures the Culture has discarded. The point concerns the established society before departure, not the reduced support available to those left behind.

Control remains with biological political and military institutions rather than being handed to independent Minds. That supports a position near the concentrated humanlike-control band, with room for collective participation. Cossont's reservist status and chosen musical life-task illustrate why a military rank need not be a full-time job. The nonworking point is a coarse, low-confidence editorial estimate of a large leisure population; it is not a number supplied by Banks. Creative and organizational work still count, which keeps the estimate below complete nonparticipation.

guarantees.basis: Long-established sufficiency for the population; vestigial exchange does not imply ordinary subsistence scarcity.

control.basis: Biological military and political organization persists; broad ownership and effective authority are not fully described.

nonworking.basis: A deliberately rough estimate from post-need life-tasks and reservist rather than universally active service; productive elective roles remain.

evidence.claim: Material sufficiency and vestigial money are explicitly distinguished.
The published setup and activity examples show biological military organization alongside chosen life-tasks.
evidence.locator: Publisher synopsis; SFRA discussion of Cossont

uncertainties: Verify the quoted primary passage against a paginated edition.
The nonworking estimate is a broad editorial judgment, not a census or an inference that every reservist is idle.
Precise ownership and constitutional control need more primary detail.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: The Algebraist (Dwellers of Nasqueron)

scope.continuity: The Algebraist; separate from the Culture universe
scope.period: Nasqueron's established Dweller order before the story's crisis
scope.population: Adult and juvenile biological Dwellers; this is an explicitly nonhuman proxy population
exclusions: Human Seers as a proxy for the native population
An assumption that adult rights also protect juveniles

societies.description:
Dweller adults can obtain mass-produced Common goods as a right of membership, without paying kudos. Prestige buys distinction, while ordinary provision does not require winning the status game. This is strong evidence for a post-work social mechanism rather than merely a wealthy visitor's experience. The positive control placement reflects decentralized civic roles and common access, with uncertainty about the machinery behind every service.

The guarantee score is much less generous than an adult-only postcard would suggest. The same novel explicitly describes adults hunting juveniles; comfortable adulthood does not secure every member's survival. Nor does the word hobby make all activity nonwork: maintaining knowledge, tailoring and administration can still involve useful effort. The nonworking fraction stays unresolved because the evidence does not establish how frequent those activities are, especially across both age groups. This alien society uses the axes by disclosed analogy, and supplies no literal human employment percentage.

guarantees.basis: Adult Common entitlement coexists with a severe age-based exclusion from security.

control.basis: Common access and varied local civic selection are visible; a sovereign AI owner is not established.

nonworking.basis: Elective professions and knowledge work remain; neither an adult nor all-age activity fraction is given.

evidence.claim: Common access is a membership entitlement rather than a reward for prestige.
Juvenile predation limits any claim of universal security.
evidence.locator: Fassin–Taince discussion and narrator's clarification, mirror page 17

uncertainties: The actual productive infrastructure needs further corroboration beyond the goods-and-hobbies mechanism.
Survival, age coverage and material entitlement are not treated as interchangeable.
AI refugees are independent actors, not assumed to be an invisible enslaved workforce.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: Consider Phlebas (Idiran Empire before defeat)

scope.period: Idiran imperial order during the Idiran-Culture War, before later machine emancipation
scope.population: Biological Idirans and their subordinate populations; a nonhuman political proxy
exclusions: A point that averages the war and postwar settlement

societies.description:
The Idiran Empire is retained as a zero-variant reference because its religious order rejects true machine autonomy despite possessing advanced technology. Political and military purposes remain those of biological rulers. This is a useful contrast with the Culture, where independent machine citizens are central to the social system. The control point is therefore near concentrated biological command rather than autonomous AI rule.

That contrast does not establish the empire's complete welfare arrangements. Its subordinate populations also prevent using an image of privileged warriors as a guarantee to everyone. Both the guarantee coordinate and the nonworking fraction remain unresolved rather than being assigned from the empire's reputation for conquest. The snapshot stops before the later changes to Idiran computer systems. A direct review of the novel's appendix is still needed to strengthen the current secondary evidence and decide whether that later order merits a separate candidate.

guarantees.basis: The gathered evidence does not establish a universal subsistence arrangement across imperial ranks and subject populations.

control.basis: Biological religious and military command rejects independent machine sovereignty.

nonworking.basis: No civilian all-population participation estimate can be grounded in the war account alone.

evidence.claim: Religious opposition to true AI provides the automation-related zero-variant connection.

uncertainties: The current classification needs primary appendix corroboration.
The secondary civilization table is not trusted for unverified economic details.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

societies.name: The Algebraist (Mercatoria)

scope.continuity: The Algebraist; not the Culture setting
scope.period: Mercatorial order before the novel's ending changes its strategic position
scope.population: Human and other biological inhabitants of the Mercatoria
exclusions: All imperial worlds assumed economically identical

societies.description:
The Mercatoria's persecution of machine intelligence makes it a zero variant with a direct technological basis. Capable AIs exist in the setting, but the imperial order seeks to prevent their open existence and authority. Production and government therefore cannot simply be described as an independent machine welfare system. The control placement remains near a concentrated biological hierarchy.

The ban is much better supported than any universal account of income or basic provision across the empire. The Dwellers' Common system belongs to a different society and is not transferred to the Mercatoria merely because both appear in one book. The guarantee and nonworking axes are left open. The novel's ending also permits hopes of political change without describing a fully enacted new economy. Such possibilities are research questions, not additional completed regimes. This entry separates an established policy toward AI from claims about everyday distribution that require further primary passages.

guarantees.basis: A machine ban and imperial hierarchy do not specify reliable material entitlements for every subject population.

control.basis: The biological hierarchy persecutes rather than enfranchises autonomous AIs.

nonworking.basis: Economic activity is not quantified in the reviewed machine-war passages.

evidence.claim: AI persecution is an established imperial policy; later compromise is an interpretation of an open ending.
evidence.locator: Machine War explanation; Martin pages 186 and 193

uncertainties: The institutional PDF could only be read in substantial indexed excerpts.
Normal labor and distribution need primary work beyond the ending exposition.

decisions.reason: Azad's hierarchy is established; a post-work mechanism or society-wide suppression of available automation is not.
decisions.analysis:
The primary briefing describes rank, sex hierarchy and the ban on unnatural assistance during Azad matches. That is relevant political evidence, but the tournament rule is not a general prohibition on AI in production. The Culture's technological superiority also belongs to the visitor's civilization, not automatically to the host economy.

Keep this candidate unresolved until primary passages establish how goods are produced and how ordinary Azadians obtain necessities. A wealthy, cruel empire is not by itself an automation scenario. The word Azad meaning machine or system must not be mistaken for evidence that machines have replaced its workers.
decisions.follow_up: Review the Imperium city tour, career system and any civilian production passages; separate a game-assistance restriction from an economic automation policy.

decisions.reason: Affront cruelty and genetic engineering are documented, but its productive and distribution arrangements remain unclear.
decisions.analysis:
The consulted material identifies an advanced civilization that mistreats subordinate beings and exploits a stolen Culture fleet. Those details establish neither the extent of routine labor automation nor an entitlement to necessities. Military machinery borrowed from another polity cannot silently supply the missing civilian economy.

Biological engineering could matter if manufactured service populations replace work by the dominant species, but that relationship needs a primary passage and an explicit population scope. Do not turn any unpleasant advanced society into regime three by default. The candidate remains a lead rather than a scored record.
decisions.follow_up: Read Excession's Affront-host scenes for actual service labor, property and subsistence rules.

decisions.reason: The candidate combines materially different caste, reform and postwar periods without sufficient economic evidence.
decisions.analysis:
The caste order changes before the disastrous war, so a single label for all Chelgrian civilization risks combining incompatible snapshots. Repression, reform and wartime loss are not themselves measures of automation or post-work access.

Choose a period only after checking civilian production and the material consequences of caste membership in Look to Windward. The afterlife system may supply another social scenario, but it is not automatically the same as the biological society or proof that living Chelgrians no longer need to work.
decisions.follow_up: Review Ziller's accounts and the pre-reform economy; append a separate afterlife candidate only if its arrangements are sufficiently described.

decisions.reason: The official synopsis supports enslavement and elite ownership, not a complete automation-based economy.
decisions.analysis:
Lededje's Intagliated status establishes a coercive personal relationship. It does not show that every citizen's livelihood has been replaced by automated output, nor that all advanced digital systems serve ordinary provision. The novel's simulated Hells are another institution with a distinct population.

A final record needs the actual civilian production and access mechanism of the Sichultian Enablement, with the enslaved and excluded population included in scope. Do not borrow the Culture's guarantees or assign universal destitution from one person's captivity. The title remains in the queue with a precise evidence gap.
decisions.follow_up: Review Veppers's industrial holdings, the meaning of Intagliated labor and ordinary household provisioning in the novel.

decisions.reason: GFCF technological level and foreign policy do not establish any of the economic axes.
decisions.analysis:
The reference identifies the GFCF as a named, technologically advanced polity in Surface Detail. That supports identifying the candidate, but provides little civilian economic information. A level-seven label does not prove universal material abundance, broad ownership or a population freed from work.

Leave its admission and coordinates unresolved. The sources presently encountered are far stronger on diplomatic behavior and conflict than on distribution. A distinct name or military capability is not sufficient reason to add another completed Culture-universe point.
decisions.follow_up: Find primary descriptions of the GFCF's economy and AI rights; exclude if the novel supplies no relevant social mechanism.

decisions.reason: A distinct biologically organized post-need society retains vestigial money and military institutions.
Morthanveld social transition and constrained AI rights are relevant, but the available reference is internally unreliable and economically incomplete.
decisions.analysis:
The narrative overview describes residual monetary exchange and an approach toward Culture-like arrangements. Its table simultaneously labels the polity as AI-ruled, making mechanical use of the summary unsafe. A quoted primary discussion encountered elsewhere indicates that full AI freedom is precisely one of the changes still at issue.

This is a promising transition candidate, but a megastructure and peer-level technology do not establish universal provision or effective ownership. Retrieve the actual Matter passage on going Culture before assigning the control axis, and look for further civilian economic detail. Do not resolve a contradiction by selecting whichever line gives an attractive coordinate.
decisions.follow_up: Read the primary Morthanveld discussion in Matter, corroborating money, AI citizenship and material access independently.

decisions.reason: Religious restriction of true AI supplies the zero-variant connection; welfare and participation remain open.
No materially distinct distribution/control mechanism has yet been established beyond the Culture economic model already recorded.
decisions.analysis:
The quoted Excession passage establishes a separate Culture-derived group with a different aim: changing itself through contact. That is a philosophical and diplomatic difference, not yet a demonstrated change in material guarantees, productive ownership or human–AI authority.

Under this project's rule against multiplying the same economic model by every faction name, retain the Elench as a related polity in the decision ledger rather than a second completed point. Reopen the decision if a primary passage demonstrates a distinct mechanism along the requested axes. The unrelated EVE corporation statistics are not lore evidence.
decisions.follow_up: Check the complete Excession context for a substantive economic or control difference before creating a separate record.

decisions.reason: Common goods are an explicit entitlement, but juvenile exclusion prevents an uncomplicated universal-utopia placement.
Systematic AI persecution preserves a biologically controlled order despite the demonstrated existence of capable machines.
Cryptosphere uploading and rescue technology do not yet establish the civilian labor and distribution system.
decisions.analysis:
Feersum Endjinn presents digital afterlives, emerging machine ecology and political conflict on a far-future Earth. These are relevant technological ingredients, but the reviewed overview does not establish what ordinary people must do to obtain food, shelter or continued support.

The physical kingdom and virtual crypt also have different inhabitants and institutions. A combined record could silently attribute the security of one realm to the other. Review the primary passages before deciding whether to split them, retain a zero variant, or exclude the work for insufficient economic description. Familiarity with the author's Culture setting supplies none of the missing facts.
decisions.follow_up: Review living-world provision and crypt maintenance/control separately, using Bascule, Gadfium and Sessine passages.

review_notes: Search results from fan fiction, generative-looking summaries and unrelated EVE game records were not treated as canon.
The Morthanveld reference table conflicts with its narrative; the contradiction remains an explicit research gap.
Gzilt nonworking is an openly low-confidence editorial estimate, not a reported statistic.
The Dweller entry includes juveniles rather than extending adult Common privileges to everyone.
The Elench is provisionally merged under the existing economic model, not asserted to be the same political organization.
